*** Windwakers new album ‘smile, you’re on camera’ will be available worldwide on Friday 23 October via Civilians & Fearless Records. Available to pre-order on vinyl and CD here: https://wind-waker.lnk.to/syoc ***
Australia's genre-bending Windwaker are thrilled to announce their 'Smile, You're On Camera' Australian headline tour for October/November where they'll be joined by special guests and first time visitors The Pretty Wild (US), as well as RinRin and DREGG.
"We are so excited to bring our new album to life on stages all around Australia," says Windwaker vocalist Liam Guinane. "We've poured so much into this record, and we can't wait to play these songs live for the very first time. We're also so stoked to be bringing out The Pretty Wild for their Australian debut, along with a couple of our favourite Aussie artists. We hope to see you all there."
The tour will begin just a week after the release of smile, you're on camera, a record that stands as the soundtrack to Windwaker's journey since HYPERVIOLENCE. Described as their most honest release yet, smile, you're on camera sees Windwaker channel the challenges and triumphs of the past few years.
The band teased this new chapter with “victory lap” and “click” (with RinRin), heightening anticipation for what's to come. Co-written in Los Angeles with the band and Daniel Braunstein (Spiritbox, Dayseeker), new single “closer” opens with strobe-flashes of neon synths and a hypnotic drumbeat, giving way to open-hearted melodies. The crunch of power chords ignites a chantable chorus, with a crushing breakdown - in true Windwaker style - that caps it all off. Watch the video here.
Joining Windwaker on their Australian headline tour are Las Vegas sisters The Pretty Wild, bringing their unpredictable mix of metal, hard rock and electronics to Australian audiences for the very first time. Their audacious spirit creates an electrifying force that defies convention. The Pretty Wild captivates audiences hungry for something different, singing of disillusionment, the struggles of the industry, and the pursuit of authenticity beyond social constructs.
'click." collaborator RinRin also joins the bill. Fusing hyperpop with alt-pop, alt-metal and pop punk, the Filipino-born, Australian-based artist has carved out a lane entirely her own. Since emerging in 2020, RinRin has shared stages with The Plot In You, Scene Queen, Caskets, and The Home Team, while also joining Walk Off The Earth for a six-city arena tour across China.
Opening all shows except Perth are fellow Melburnians and Fearless Records labelmates DREGG. Known for their high-energy fusion of metal, hardcore and rap, their music, visuals, and over-the-top personas serve as a satirical lens on modern culture. Blending shock value with deeper commentary, DREGG encourages fans to embrace their inner weirdos and challenge societal norms through unapologetic self-expression.

Sacramento post-hardcore mainstays Dance Gavin Dance have announced an Australian headline tour for this November, joined by special guests and fellow post-hardcore veterans The Fall of Troy and Australian-led rockers Galleons.
The tour arrives in celebration of Dance Gavin Dance’s latest album, Pantheon, while also deep diving into their celebrated back catalogue. Kicking off at The Tivoli in Brisbane on Friday 6 November, the run will then head to Enmore Theatre in Sydney on Saturday 7 November, Forum in Melbourne on Sunday 8 November, The Gov in Adelaide on Tuesday 10 November, before wrapping up at Freo Social in Perth on Thursday 12 November.
Formed in Sacramento, California in 2005, Dance Gavin Dance - comprised of vocalist/guitarist Andrew Wells, co-vocalist Jon Mess, guitarist Will Swan and drummer Matthew Mingus - have long stood as one of alternative music’s most distinctive acts. A powerhouse of alternative music; true originals and originators alike, Dance Gavin Dance craft an exhilarating cacophony of sounds and disparate styles that harmonises everything from funk through metalcore to post-hardcore, pop sensibilities colliding with progressive, kaleidoscopic song structures.
With four Billboard 200 Top 15 albums to their name, millions of records sold, billions of streams, and one of the most devoted fanbases in modern heavy music, Dance Gavin Dance are as at home on the world’s most famous stages as they are hosting their own culture-defining annual festival, Swanfest. As the esteemed Rock Sound magazine attests: "There is no band on earth like Dance Gavin Dance."
Joining the Cali legends on the Australian run are The Fall of Troy, a musical force that has been pushing the boundaries of math rock since their formation in 2002. Hailing from Mukilteo, Washington, the band first made waves with their 2005 albupelgänger, which showcased their signature blend of technical proficiency and energy. Over the years, The Fall of Troy has continued to evolve, exploring new territory and challenging the very notions of time and structure. With each new release, they have cemented their place as one of the most innovative and daring bands in the world of math rock.
Completing the bill are Galleons, a band born out of a transcontinental collaboration between Australian and Eastern European musicians with a sound that effortlessly blends post-hardcore and math rock with a multitude of adjacent and disconnected genres. In the last decade Galleons has done their very best to solidify their place in the heavy music scene while collaborating with prominent musicians from iconic post-hardcore and alternative bands. Their captivating energy and love for the genre continues in its attempts to push boundaries and redefine what post-hardcore means to them and others.

*** Northlane’s new album ‘Anemoia’ will be available worldwide on Friday 30 October. Available to pre-order on vinyl and CD here: https://au.northlaneband.com/ ***
Australian heavy music trailblazers, Northlane will embark on their biggest Australian headline this November with the Anemoia Tour joined by special guests After The Burial (usa), Cenobia + Above, Below.
Following on from their #1 album Obsidian (2022), Anemoia toys with the concept of feeling nostalgia for a time or place one has never known. This yearning opens up a dichotomy of darkness and light, where the sense of freedom of eras past buoys a carefree energy running through tracks like first single "Evian", while feelings of anger and despair come roaring back when the present day shatters the reverie, leading to some of Northlane’s heaviest moments since their first EP.
Across a career defined by seismic shifts, Northlane have stared down technological anxiety, alienation and collapse, channelling it into a highly influential body of work that is as expansive as it is confrontational. With the world in dire straits, it would have been easy for them to descend into the void on album number seven. Instead, they emerged from the studio with their most hopeful and human record yet.
More than 15 years into their career, Northlane continue to stand at the forefront of heavy music globally with a singular sound that shifts the genre’s landscape with every release. With multiple chart-topping albums, awards and over 500 million streams, the band has built a legacy defined by the restless pursuit of innovation. On Anemoia, they have not chosen between the worlds that shaped them - they have finally found where they meet.
Metalcore pioneers, After The Burial from Minneapolis will make their long awaited return back to Australia. Since their last visit down under back in 2019 when they supported Make Them Suffer, the band have been carving away with new material, Going on a hiatus for four years, the band returned with strength with a two track single 'Embrace The Inifinity' in 2023 and their latest offering with Hum From The Hollow in 2025.
Cenobia, the mysterious artist who bursted into the music scene back in 2025. With her debut single 'Devour Me' accumulating million of streams across streaming platforms then following it up from strength to strength with 'Throne Of Want' and 'Make Us Whole Again'. Once awoken from her slumber, she announced her debut performance at Oxford Art Factory that sold out within minutes and left all fans wanting more.
Rounding out the bill will be South-Eastern Sydney siders in Above, Below who have received massive praise from heavy music fans with their sophomore album 'I Guess It Was Nowhere'. This will be the bands first time performing these songs live and will be the first tour they have done across the country since supporting US Metalcore giants in Silent Planet and Currents back in 2022.

In a time of digital chaos and concrete sprawl, the frequencies have locked in and a citadel for heavy and alternative music will emerge once again in 2026. Welcome to the next evolution of Australia’s largest travelling music celebration, with Good Things Festival returning this year for another monumental cycle, armed with a colossal lineup from every sector, spanning culture-shaping legends through to the current defining generation of the alternative scene and emerging artists set to shape the future. Locked in across the East Coast this December, all event dates will once again be 16+ and up. The network is alive, and the architectural soundscape awaits to welcome all generations in Melbourne, Sydney and Brisbane this December.
Leading the primary frequency for Good Things Festival in 2026, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧’s imprint on nu metal and alternative culture has generated an enduring and towering reputation throughout the band’s 30+ year career. As one of the major pioneers of nu metal, and one of the most successful bands in the scene of all time, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧’s signature collision of rap rock, grooves, searing riffs, angsty themes and larger than life performances has transcended the group from the late 90s breeding ground of MTV and teenage frustrations into enamouring a multi-generational fanbase with high octane party anthems and entertaining chaos decades since their formation. Exploding out of the gates with their debut full-length album, 1997’s 𝙏𝙝𝙧𝙚𝙚 𝘿𝙤𝙡𝙡𝙖𝙧 𝘽𝙞𝙡𝙡, 𝙔’𝙖𝙡𝙡, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧’s sophomore 1999 album 𝙎𝙞𝙜𝙣𝙞𝙛𝙞𝙘𝙖𝙣𝙩 𝙊𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙧 reached #1 on the US Billboard 200, ticked off two 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗠𝗬 Award Nominations, was certified 7 x Platinum, and spawned some of the band’s perennially adored singles, including 𝘉𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘬 𝘚𝘵𝘶𝘧𝘧 and 𝘕𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘪𝘦. Now with six studio albums under their belts, including 2000’s 𝘾𝙝𝙤𝙘𝙤𝙡𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙧𝙛𝙞𝙨𝙝 𝙖𝙣𝙙 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙃𝙤𝙩 𝘿𝙤𝙜 𝙁𝙡𝙖𝙫𝙤𝙧𝙚𝙙 𝙒𝙖𝙩𝙚𝙧 which set the record for the fastest-selling rock album of all time, and their most recent full-length venture, 2021’s 𝙎𝙏𝙄𝙇𝙇 𝙎𝙐𝘾𝙆𝙎, 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 continue to blitz streaming charts to this very day, sell out international tours and headline powerhouse global festivals, including Download Festival earlier this year. 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 will make their return to Good Things Festival in 2026 as headliners following their unforgettable performances at the 2023 edition and selling out their headline sideshows in Brisbane and Melbourne. Believe the hype, there’s nothing quite like a 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗣 𝗕𝗜𝗭𝗞𝗜𝗧 live show, and these will be monolithic performances to truly rattle the mainframe.
As one of the most culturally and commercially successful bands in rock, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have spent over two decades cultivating and evolving their status as pop punk legends. Now in command of over 10 billion streams worldwide, almost 2 billion views on YouTube, and an inescapable social media presence that bridges their longtime fans with a whole new generation, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have never been a band content to rest on their laurels. Famous for their buoyant performances laden with pop punk anthems and infectious enthusiasm, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 have also raised more than $3 million through their Simple Plan Foundation over the years. Recently celebrating their 25th anniversary in 2025, including a co-headline run with The Offspring down under, 𝗦𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡 will once again wow Good Things Festival crowds in 2026 after their mesmerising appearances at the event in 2019.
The sonic equivalent of capturing lightning in a bottle, Canada’s 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫 solidified themselves as a household name in 2020 via their blistering breakout single 𝘏𝘰𝘭𝘺 𝘙𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘳. Instantly capturing attention and exploding into a meteoric rise, the progressive heavy metal mainstays have notably never plateaued along the way, exceeding every expectation in 2021 with the release of their debut studio album 𝙀𝙩𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙖𝙡 𝘽𝙡𝙪𝙚, which debuted at #13 on the US Billboard 200, and ultimately rewrote the genre’s playbook in the process. With three 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗠𝗠𝗬 Award nominations under their belts for Best Metal Performance, including for 𝘑𝘢𝘥𝘦𝘥 in 2024, 𝘊𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘢𝘳 𝘋𝘰𝘰𝘳 in 2025 and 𝘚𝘰𝘧𝘵 𝘚𝘱𝘪𝘯𝘦 in 2026, 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫 remain one of the most influential acts in modern metal today; a fact echoed by the band’s equally beloved 2025 sophomore studio album 𝙏𝙨𝙪𝙣𝙖𝙢𝙞 𝙎𝙚𝙖, which hit #26 on the US Billboard 200, cracked the top 20 in the UK charts, reached #1 on the UK Indie charts and #12 on the Top German Album charts. A band simultaneously capable of boundless innovation, fearless reinvention and an unwavering connection to their burgeoning global audience, 𝗦𝗣𝗜𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗕𝗢𝗫’s live show boasts arena-level production, skull-crushing heaviness morphed alongside ethereal atmospherics, while immersing audiences head-first into the band’s unwavering energy and artistry that most recently was on display for audiences down under when the group made their debut Aussie performances at Knotfest Australia in 2023.
Also feeding the Good Things Festival matrix in 2026, Sydney’s 𝗣𝗢𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗦 are primed to stupefy with their blend of ferocity and melody, laced with blistering metalcore, post-rock and electronic influences. After relentless touring over the past few years, including supporting Linkin Park earlier this year for a massive national Australian arena run and supporting Electric Callboy in North America, 𝗣𝗢𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗦 will celebrate a range of hits with Good Things audiences later this year, including cuts from their most recent 𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗔 Award-nominated studio album 𝙁𝙖𝙩𝙖𝙡𝙞𝙨𝙢 which debuted at #1 on the 𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗔 Charts, secured triple j’s Feature Album upon release and won Best Independent Heavy Album at the 2024 𝗔𝗜𝗥 Awards.
